prompt: Research concrete kernel and compiler strategies for short-budget small-language-model TRAINING on AWS Trainium2 (NeuronCore-v3, NKI 0.5, TorchNeuron native torch.compile backend, SDK 2.26, 4 logical cores LNC2). Use only primary sources: AWS Neuron/NKI docs and source repositories, research papers and their authors code. Distinguish Trainium2 from Trainium3, legacy XLA from native. Goal: lower held-out bits per byte after 1800 charged training seconds for dense decoder 6 layers x width1024, head128, vocabulary8192, sequence1024, 32768 tokens per local microbatch, Muon for matrices, AdamW for others. No external packages, pretrained weights, data or lookup dictionaries allowed; fixed tokenizer and trusted autoregressive scoring. Existing experiments: custom exact CE/gather and optimizer ownership won; full NKI FP8 MLP forward+four backward GEMMs (per-token causal scales, FP32 masters, refreshed dual packed weight caches) is 3% faster in isolation but full step slower 563ms vs489ms BF16. Caller trace shows surrounding BF16 matrix tiles shrinking and spilling, attribution incomplete. Removing unused BF16 saved outputs, streaming FP8 weights, rank3 output did not recover regression. BF16 QKV fusion preserving separate Parameters is 5-10% slower isolated; numerical integration differs with value embeddings due to graph/precision interactions even though separate replacement is exact. Need ranked hypotheses for (1) broader FP8 projection coverage or backward-first FP8; (2) compiler partition/fusion/resource boundaries and custom op autograd limitations; (3) eliminate memory traffic/collectives/optimizer work via ownership and scheduling, respecting genuine whole-step costs; (4) model/data/optimizer changes worth revisiting ONLY with a concrete confound or changed condition. Avoid seed sweeps, generation-only speculative decoding, external assets, and naive GPU-to-Trainium port assumptions. For each propose falsifiable minimum experiment, correctness/causality checks, expected bottleneck evidence, stop criterion, and direct supporting URLs. Mark suggestions unsupported by native SDK docs as hypotheses. Do not invent APIs or performance wins.
scope: public technical research; no credentials or host identities
